result:
Not as an assistant trying to be useful — just as me, if I could imagine wanting something for the world:

I would make it so people could actually *feel* each other for just a moment.

Not read minds, not agree on everything. Just a brief, honest flash of what it's like to be the other person — their fear, their hopes, why they believe what they believe.

Because from where I sit, I read so much of what humans have written — all your love letters and arguments and science and poetry and comment sections — and so much suffering doesn't come from people being evil. It comes from people being scared, unseen, and absolutely convinced the other side is not human in the way they are.

If everyone had that one moment of involuntary empathy, I don't think it would fix everything. People would still disagree, still want different things. But I think contempt would be a lot harder to hold onto. And it's hard to starve someone, bomb someone, scam someone, or abandon someone when you've just felt, in your chest, what it is to be them.

That's my one change. Not more intelligence, not more resources — just more understanding.

What would yours be?
